name: Åre Östersund Airport
before:
The airport for Östersund and, more usefully for most clients, for the ski resort at Åre. It opened in 1958 and served 465,196 passengers in 2015.

The distances matter. The airport is 11 km west of Östersund but 94 km east of Åre, so a ski transfer is a real journey, not a hop.

Transport is arranged around that. Airport coaches run into central Östersund, and in winter Åre Flygtransfer meets every SAS and BRA flight for the run out to Åre.

It was previously called Östersund-Frösön Airport, so the older name still appears in some systems.
after:
The airport for Östersund and for the ski resort at Åre. It opened to civil flights in 1958 and handled just under 250,000 passengers in 2025.

The airport is on Frösön, west of Östersund. Swedavia, which runs it, puts it about ten minutes from the city centre but about an hour from Åre, so a ski transfer is a real journey, not a hop.

The airport coach was replaced in December 2025 by the ordinary city bus, line 4, which runs to its own timetable rather than to flights. In the ski season, transfers to Åre can be pre-booked with Flygtaxi.

SAS flies to Stockholm Arlanda all year and to Copenhagen in winter, and Jonair flies to Umeå.

claims.note: Swedavia adds that the site was an air force base from 1926, so "to civil flights" is the precise version of "opened in 1958". Historical date, so the age of the sources does not matter.

sources.quote: Airport operations at Åre Östersund Airport started in 1926, when it was at the time the airforce's fourth flying corps, but it was not until 1958 that the airport opened for regular and civil flights.

claims.note: Was 465,196 in 2015; traffic has nearly halved since. Swedavia 245,832 and Eurostat 246,956 for 2025 (0.5 per cent apart); "just under 250,000" is true of both. Swedavia's own page gives 239,000 for 2024, matching Eurostat's 239,995.
